methodology.time_basis: simulated seconds; figure labels use simulated milliseconds

statistics.quantiles: Unsmoothed NumPy linear sample percentiles among committed operations.
statistics.bootstrap: 2000 independent-seed block resamples; all operations and failures within each seed retained. Pointwise 95% percentile intervals, conditional on nonempty successful samples for latency.
statistics.p99: Descriptive sample estimate; offered attempt count is not successful sample count. The bootstrap cannot establish an unobserved tail or remove timeout censoring.
statistics.figure_interval: Shading is the pointwise p95 latency 95% bootstrap interval; other interval values are preserved in JSON.

latency.workload: 5 sequential offered SET write attempts per seed per condition
latency.measurement: Proposal to first observed commitment of the exact entry; success can be observed after leadership change. No client retries.
latency.failures: Timeout and no-leader outcomes are excluded from successful latency percentiles but counted in the success denominator.
latency.loss_model: Each sent request or response independently dropped; applies during elections and workload.

elections.measurement: Startup/failure to every live node recognizing the highest-term leader; 3-second timeout.
elections.rpc_count: Sent protocol messages including responses and messages addressed to crashed nodes.
elections.split_vote: Term with at least two candidacies and no elected leader observed by convergence.
elections.workload: Election and initial no-op only; then crash the leader.

recovery.measurement: Crash/minority partition to new majority write committed; healing/restart to identical full logs, commit indexes and state machines.
recovery.timeouts: Up to 3 seconds for leader discovery plus 3 seconds for commit; 3 seconds for full convergence.
recovery.partition: Old leader plus one follower isolated from remaining three; minority write remains uncommitted.
recovery.restart_backlog: Eight SET commands while one follower is crashed.

limitations: Discrete-event measurements are not physical-network or Python throughput benchmarks.
Finite independent seeds; p99 estimates with small samples are descriptive, not precise tail guarantees.
Paired seed numbers across conditions do not imply identical random draws after fault paths diverge.
Successful latency is conditional on success and is subject to timeout censoring.
